settings_description: These change how your hours are counted and shown. They are kept on this device only.
settings_schedule_description: How many hours a full day is, and which time zone decides when a day starts.
time_zone_description: An entry logged late at night belongs to the day it was still, here.
theme_switch_to_dark: Switch to the dark colour scheme
theme_switch_to_light: Switch to the light colour scheme
dashboard_still_loading: Still loading older entries, so this may rise.
report_failed_unauthorized: GitLab no longer accepts this session. Sign in again to refresh these figures.
report_failed_unavailable: GitLab could not be reached. These figures are the last ones loaded.
report_failed_rejected: GitLab refused the request. These figures are the last ones loaded.
sign_in_description: This dashboard reads the hours you logged in GitLab, using your own account. It asks for read-only access and never writes anything back.
sign_in_no_token_notice: There is nothing to paste. You sign in with GitLab itself.
sign_in_failed_denied: You did not grant access, so there is nothing to show yet.
sign_in_failed_state_mismatch: This sign-in could not be verified as one you started. Nothing was signed in.
sign_in_failed_expired: That sign-in link is no longer valid.
sign_in_failed_unavailable: GitLab could not be reached. Nothing was signed in.
not_configured_title: This build has no GitLab application
not_configured_description: The dashboard needs the Application ID of an OAuth application in your own GitLab account. It is a public value: there is no secret to protect.
not_configured_step_create: In GitLab, open User Settings, then Applications, and add a new application.
not_configured_step_public: Leave Confidential unchecked and tick the read_api scope only.
not_configured_step_env: Put the Application ID in VITE_GITLAB_CLIENT_ID and rebuild.
